data.name: Oman
data.summary: In tax year 2026 Oman has no personal income tax, no capital gains, dividend, inheritance, gift or wealth tax for individuals. But a Personal Income Tax Law has been ENACTED (Royal Decree 56/2025) and takes effect 1 January 2028: 5% on worldwide income (including foreign dividends and gains on shares and real estate) above OMR 42,000 for residents, with exemptions for Muscat-listed shares, the main residence, and inheritances/gifts between spouses and first-degree relatives. Corporate tax 15%; dividend/interest WHT suspended; VAT 5%.

regimes.name: Oman tax residence
regimes.description: 2026: no personal taxes. Enacted 5% PIT on income above OMR 42,000 from 2028.

capital_gains.summary: 2026: no capital gains tax for individuals. From 1 January 2028 the enacted PIT will tax gains on shares, bonds and real estate at 5% above OMR 42,000 of total taxable income (Muscat-listed shares and main residence exempt).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: ENACTED, NOT YET IN FORCE: Royal Decree 56/2025 (issued 22 June 2025, gazetted 30 June 2025) promulgates a Personal Income Tax Law effective 1 January 2028: 5% on taxable income above OMR 42,000 a year, on worldwide income of tax residents (Omani citizens and expatriates present 183+ days). Taxable categories include returns from stocks, shares and bonds and from their disposal, interest, and gains on real estate. Exemptions include income and disposal proceeds of shares listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange and government bonds, main residence (conditions), one secondary residence once in a lifetime, and inheritances, grants and donations between spouses and first-degree relatives. Executive Regulations are still awaited. From 2028 a wealthy resident would pay up to 5% on foreign dividends and gains above OMR 42,000.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. The 2028 PIT exempts inheritances, grants and donations between spouses and first-degree relatives.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Succession, not tax, is the issue: personal status (family) law based on Sharia governs inheritance of Muslims, with fixed shares (a son typically takes twice a daughter's share) and at most one third freely disposable by will to non-heirs. How estates of non-Muslim foreigners are handled (home-country law, own religious rules, or Sharia by default) was not verified for this country; non-Muslim families should take local legal advice and hold portfolio assets outside the country or through a structure with a clear governing law. Under the 2028 PIT, 'grants and donations' from persons other than spouses and first-degree relatives are listed as taxable income.

income.name: Oman

income_tax.summary: Scored on the law in force for 2026: Oman levies no personal income tax in 2026. A personal income tax takes effect on 1 January 2028 (5% on annual income above OMR 42,000 after eligible deductions, worldwide income for residents), so it does not enter the 2026 scoring. Only Omani employees pay social insurance (8%); no expat employee contribution is listed.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: No self-employment contributions apply to expatriates in the sources found. From 2028, residents including expatriates are taxed at 5% above OMR 42,000 a year.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income-based taxes. For Omani employees, retirement contributions use a subscription wage ceiling (initially OMR 3,000).

succession.name: Oman
succession.summary: Muslim estates follow Ibadi Sharia rules under the Personal Status Law, with fixed shares. Courts generally honour a non-Muslim expatriate's will made under their home law, but judges have wide discretion. No source on trusts or foundations was found.
succession.reserved_share: Muslims: fixed shares under the Personal Status Law (Royal Decree 32/97, reported by secondary guide); Ibadi rules bar inheritance between Muslims and non-Muslims.
succession.foreign_law_note: Practitioners report that Omani courts generally honour wills made under a non-Muslim expatriate's home law and do not usually apply Sharia to non-Muslims, but judges have wide discretion and may distribute otherwise. Bank accounts, including joint ones, are frozen until distribution.
succession.trust_note: No trust or private-foundation statute was found for Oman; both answers are provisional.
open_questions: Royal Decree 32/97 and the Civil Transactions Law conflict rule not retrieved.
Trusts and foundations in Oman not sourced.
Oman's own non-Muslim wills procedure (if any) not confirmed.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.

immigration.name: Oman
immigration.summary: No free movement for anyone; EU, US and other passports use the same routes. The Golden Residency programme (relaunched 31 August 2025, run through Invest Oman) gives 5 years for OMR 250,000 in an investment or property, or 10 years for OMR 500,000; retirees can qualify with OMR 4,000 a month. Foreign owners of qualifying property can also get an Owner Residence Permit. No remote-work visa was confirmed. Personal income tax starts in 2028.
immigration.naturalisation: Not researched in this pass. The golden residency does not give a claim to citizenship (Gulf News: beneficiaries cannot claim Omani citizenship).
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: General rule, not verified in this pass: Oman does not generally allow dual nationality.

routes.name: Golden Residency - 10 years
routes.summary: A 10-year renewable residence for investing OMR 500,000, buying OMR 500,000 of property, or creating a company with 50 Omani employees.
routes.requirements: Any one of: OMR 500,000 in an Omani LLC, public joint-stock company or government bonds; property worth OMR 500,000; a company employing at least 50 Omanis. Age 21+, valid health insurance. Applications through the Invest Oman platform. Program relaunched 31 August 2025 (Deloitte). Observer reports describe a lower RO 200,000 entry; unconfirmed.
routes.investment_options: Alternative with no capital minimum: company employing at least 50 Omanis.
routes.fees_note: Gulf News (Sep 2025): OMR 551. The 2021 programme fee for the principal investor was OMR 500 (Fragomen), so the current fee is unconfirmed.
routes.tax_note: No personal income tax until a 5% tax on income above OMR 42,000 starts in 2028 (Royal Decree 56/2025).
